conceptPrimer.heading: Photon Quanta: Energy and Momentum Packets
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Light of frequency $\nu$ (wavelength $\lambda$) travels as photons, each carrying energy $E = h\nu = \frac{hc}{\lambda} \approx \frac{1240\ \text{eV\,nm}}{\lambda(\text{nm})}$ and momentum $p = \frac{h}{\lambda} = \frac{E}{c}$ (rest mass zero). The $1240$ shortcut converts any wavelength to eV in one division. A beam's intensity is photon energy per second — more photons, not stronger photons. Micro-check: $\lambda = 620\ \text{nm}$ gives $E = \tfrac{1240}{620} = 2\ \text{eV}$ per photon.

conceptPrimer.heading: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation
conceptPrimer.proseLatex:
One photon liberates at most one electron, spending the work function $\phi_0$ (the metal's escape price) and handing the surplus to kinetic energy: $K_{\max} = h
u - \phi_0$. No light below threshold $
u_0 =  rac{\phi_0}{h}$ can eject electrons, however intense. The stopping potential measures $K_{\max}$ in volts: $eV_s = K_{\max}$. Micro-check: $h
u = 4\ 	ext{eV}$ onto a $\phi_0 = 1.5\ 	ext{eV}$ metal gives $K_{\max} = 2.5\ 	ext{eV}$ and $V_s = 2.5\ 	ext{V}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Intensity vs Frequency: Who Controls What
conceptPrimer.proseLatex:
Above threshold, raising INTENSITY (fixed $
u$) sends more photons per second, so the saturation photocurrent grows linearly — $K_{\max}$ and $V_s$ do NOT move. Raising FREQUENCY moves the energy ladder: $K_{\max} = h
u - \phi_0$ grows, and doubling $
u$ gives $K_{\max}' = 2h
u - \phi_0 = 2K_{\max} + \phi_0$, STRICTLY more than double. Graph trap: $V_s$ vs $
u$ has slope $ rac{h}{e}$; $K_{\max}$ vs $
u$ has slope $h$. Micro-check: $K_{\max} = 1\ 	ext{eV}$, $\phi_0 = 1\ 	ext{eV}$: doubling $
u$ yields $2(1) + 1 = 3\ 	ext{eV}$, not $2\ 	ext{eV}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Threshold in Two Currencies
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: The threshold can be written as a frequency $\nu_0 = \frac{\phi_0}{h}$ or as the longest ejecting wavelength $\lambda_0 = \frac{1240\ \text{eV\,nm}}{\phi_0(\text{eV})}$ (nm). Wavelengths LONGER than $\lambda_0$ fail regardless of intensity. Compute one currency, convert with the $1240$ shortcut. Micro-check: $\phi_0 = 3\ \text{eV}$ gives $\lambda_0 \approx \tfrac{1240}{3} \approx 413\ \text{nm}$ — visible violet edge.

conceptPrimer.heading: de Broglie: Matter Wears the Same Wave Coat
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Every moving particle has wavelength $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$; an electron accelerated from rest through $V$ volts gains $K = eV$ and shows $\lambda(\text{\AA}) \approx \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}$. Faster particles carry SHORTER waves — the same inverse logic as photons. Micro-check: electrons through $100\ \text{V}$ have $\lambda = \tfrac{12.27}{10} \approx 1.23\ \text{\AA}$, matching crystal lattice spacings — why Davisson-Germer saw diffraction.

conceptPrimer.heading: Photocell Bookkeeping and the Solar Cell
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Photon arrival rate is power divided by photon energy: $\dot{N} = \frac{P_{\text{in}}}{E}$. In a photocircuit, electrons between $K_{\max}$ and $0$ are emitted; the stopping potential just stops the fastest. A solar PHOTovoltaic cell converts photon energy DIRECTLY into electrical energy across a p-n junction — no external battery — output scaling with irradiance. Micro-check: a $2\ \text{W}$ beam of $2\ \text{eV}$ photons delivers $\frac{2}{2 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}} = 6.25 \times 10^{18}$ photons per second.

keyDefinitions.definition: A quantum of light: energy $h\nu$, momentum $h/\lambda$, zero rest mass.
The minimum energy to free an electron from a metal surface; varies by metal.
$\nu_0 = \phi_0/h$ — the lowest frequency that can eject photoelectrons.
The retarding voltage that just halts the fastest photoelectrons: $eV_s = K_{\max}$.
The plateau photocurrent when every emitted electron is collected; scales with intensity.
Ejection of electrons from a metal by light of frequency above threshold.
The matter-wave length $h/p$ attached to any moving particle.
Charge emitted per second reaching the collector; zero below threshold.
A p-n junction converting photon energy directly into electrical energy without an external bias.
Energy per unit area per second — a photon COUNT property, not a per-photon energy.

memoryHooks: $1240$ nm-eV: divide by wavelength, get electron-volts.
One photon buys one electron: pay $\phi_0$, keep the change as $K_{\max}$.
Intensity hires MORE photons; frequency arms EACH photon.
Doubling $\nu$ more than doubles $K_{\max}$: the bonus is exactly $\phi_0$.
No threshold, no electrons — intensity is powerless below $\nu_0$.
$V_s$ graph slopes $h/e$; $K_{\max}$ graph slopes $h$ — check the axis.
Faster matter, shorter wave: $\lambda = 12.27/\sqrt{V}$ for electrons.
Photon rate = power split by packet size.
Stopping potential is $K_{\max}$ read in volts.
Solar cell = photovoltaic junction, not electron emission into air.
commonMistakes: Doubling $K_{\max}$ when frequency doubles — the true new value is $2K_{\max} + \phi_0$.
Raising $K_{\max}$ or $V_s$ with intensity — intensity only feeds current.
Sloping the $V_s$-$\nu$ graph with $h$ instead of $h/e$.
Expecting photoemission below threshold by cranking intensity.
Feeding nanometres where metres belong, or eV where joules belong — units first.
Using $p = mc$ for photons — their momentum is $E/c$ with zero rest mass.
Reading $\sqrt{V}$ as $V$ in the electron de Broglie shortcut.
Counting photon rates with $P \times E$ instead of $P/E$.
Confusing the emission photocell with the photovoltaic solar cell.
examChecklist: Convert wavelength to eV with the 1240 shortcut before any equation.
Stopping potential numerics: $V_s = K_{\max}/e$ in volts.
Intensity questions: answer with saturation current, never $K_{\max}$.
Graph questions: identify which of $V_s$ or $K_{\max}$ is plotted, then pick $h/e$ or $h$.
de Broglie numerics: $12.27/\sqrt{V}$ for electrons; $h/p$ otherwise.
Photon-rate questions divide power by per-photon energy.
Threshold questions: choose $\nu_0 = \phi_0/h$ or $\lambda_0 = 1240/\phi_0$ to match the ask.
Carry eV and joules separately; convert with $1\ \text{eV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ \text{J}$.
Re-verify one energy audit: photon in = escape price + kinetic out.
